summary: This bill abolishes the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations within the Department of Energy and repeals the section of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act that established it.

scores.thoughts: The bill abolishes the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (OCED) within the Department of Energy and repeals Section 41201 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which established OCED and authorized significant funding (around $8 billion) for clean energy demonstration projects. This directly eliminates a federal program involving government spending on clean energy initiatives, thereby reducing government spending. The impact is clear and substantial for this specific area, warranting a large positive score.
The bill makes no mention of taxes, tax rates, tax policies, or any revenue-raising or reduction measures. It solely addresses the abolition of a Department of Energy office.
The bill does not reference healthcare, medical coverage, insurance, or any health-related programs. It is focused on energy policy.
No provisions related to firearms, gun rights, regulations, or Second Amendment issues appear in the bill.
The bill has no content concerning immigration, borders, visas, or protections for immigrants.
The bill does not address abortion, reproductive rights, or related healthcare policies.
The bill targets a civilian Department of Energy office unrelated to military or defense spending, procurement, or operations.

OCED was created to fund and demonstrate clean energy technologies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and advancing climate goals. Abolishing it and repealing its authorizing statute removes federal government support for these environmental initiatives, limiting proactive environmental protections and clean energy development efforts. This has a moderate to strong alignment with limiting environmental regulations and interventions.
No references to welfare, food stamps, unemployment benefits, or other social safety net programs.
The bill does not involve schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policies.
No content on drugs, decriminalization, enforcement, or substance abuse policies.
The bill lacks any provisions on policing, sentencing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
No mentions of trade agreements, tariffs, protectionism, or international commerce.

By abolishing OCED and repealing its funding authorization, the bill eliminates ongoing federal expenditures (originally $8 billion), which indirectly supports deficit reduction and debt management. However, it is a specific cut rather than a broad debt prioritization measure, so the impact is tangential.
The bill does not address LGBTQ+ protections, discrimination, or related rights.
No provisions related to foreign assistance, international aid, or overseas spending.
The bill has no connection to voting access, elections, voter ID, or electoral processes.
While clean energy may involve technology, the bill does not address tech regulation, data privacy, surveillance, or oversight of tech companies.
No content on labor rights, unions, worker protections, or employer regulations.
The bill does not involve religious exemptions, anti-discrimination laws, or civil rights protections.

The bill abolishes the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations and repeals its authorizing provision, directly eliminating the associated federal spending and outlays. This narrow, single-purpose legislation is centrally about removing a spending program.
